checkpoints.title: Tradeoff duel
checkpoints.prompt: 10B pages in 5 days. What governs the fetch order?

options.label: One global URL queue
options.verdict: Simple, and it will get you blocked within the hour. A breadth-first frontier naturally clusters many URLs from the same host together, so you hammer one origin while the rest of the internet idles.

options.label: Per-host queues with politeness
options.sub: one worker per host, backoff on 429
options.verdict: Politeness is a per-host property, so the queue has to be per-host too. Throughput comes from crawling many hosts concurrently, not from crawling one host quickly.

defend.prompt: What does per-host queueing force you to handle?

options.label: Rebalancing when one host has millions of URLs
Honouring robots.txt and Crawl-delay per host
Jittered exponential backoff after a 429 or 503

defend.explain: Discovery order is unchanged — you still find URLs breadth-first, you just fetch them politely. The new work is per-host scheduling, robots caching, and backoff with jitter so retries do not resynchronise into a thundering herd.

checkpoints.title: Capacity ladder
checkpoints.prompt: 10B pages in 5 days, roughly 2 MB of HTML each.

rungs.note: 10B / (5 x 86,400). Peak has to exceed this, since no crawl runs flat.
10B x 2 MB. Text extract is far smaller, but the raw fetch still crosses the wire.

choices: Extract text, discard most raw HTML
rungs.note: At 20 PB you keep the extract and a sample, not every byte you fetched.

checkpoints.explain: 23k pages/sec is a concurrency problem, not a bandwidth problem — it is thousands of hosts in flight at once, each politely slow.

checkpoints.title: Architecture builder
checkpoints.prompt: Build the crawl loop from frontier to stored text.
checkpoints.explain: The scheduler sits between the frontier and the fetchers because politeness is what decides when a URL may be fetched, not what is next in line. Dedup runs before storage so near-identical pages never reach it. The robots and DNS caches serve the fetcher; they are not stages of the pipeline.

checkpoints.title: Spot the bottleneck
checkpoints.prompt: Crawl rate collapsed from 23k to 4k pages/sec. Error rate is climbing.
checkpoints.explain: Fetcher utilisation fell, which means workers are idle — they are blocked, not busy. The DNS cache hit rate collapsed, so most fetches now wait on a fresh resolution before a single byte moves. A crawler is one of the few systems where DNS is on the hot path for every request, which is why the resolver cache is infrastructure and not an optimisation.

wrong.Fetcher pool: Low utilisation is the symptom of blocked workers. Ask what they are waiting on.
wrong.URL Frontier: There is plenty of work queued — that is the opposite of a bottleneck.
wrong.Content Store: Writes are fast, and there are fewer of them than before.
